See AMC.1329 (e), AMC.1329 (i) and AMC.1329 (j) The flight control system comprises sensors, actuators, computers and all those elements of the UAV System, necessary to control the attitude, speed and trajectory of the UAV. The flight control system must meet the following:
(a) The modes of control of the UAV must be the following categories, which may be selected at any time in flight by the UAV crew:
  (1) automatic : in this mode the UAV attitude, speed and flight path are fully controlled by the flight control system. No input from the UCS is needed other than to load or modify the required flight plan.
  (2) semi-automatic : with this type of control the UAV crew commands outer loop parameters such as altitude, heading and air speed. The flight control system operates the UAV controls to achieve the commanded outer loop parameter value.
(b) The flight control system must be designed so that a UAV crew of average skill can operate the UAV System with acceptable workload,
(c) The flight control system must apply limits to manoeuvres to keep the UAV in the flight envelope protection as defined in USAR.334
(d) The UAV crews must have the opportunity to intervene at any time during the flight to manage safe control of the UAV, except :
  (1) during emergency situations such as total loss of data link, (2) during launch phase before achieving the minimum safe flight parameters, (3) during landing phase after reaching the decision point as defined in USAR.1490 and USAR.1492, (4) for UAV designed to be recovered by parachute, during the landing phase under parachute, (5) for rocket or catapult assisted take-off UAV, during the launch phase before reaching the limits specified in USAR.282.
(e) The flight control system must be designed and adjusted so that, within the range of adjustment (if any) available to UAV crew, it cannot produce an unsafe condition.
(f) The flight control system must be designed so that a single malfunction will not produce a hardover signal in more than one control axis except if the effect of this malfunction is lower or equal to a minor failure severity. If the flight control system integrates signals from auxiliary controls or furnishes signals for operation of other equipment, positive interlocks and sequencing of engagement to prevent improper operation are required.
(g) There must be protection against adverse interaction of integrated components, resulting from a malfunction.
(h) Not applicable in this subpart (see USAR.1790 UAV mode of control indicator)
(i) Use of active flight controls for load alleviation, stability augmentation, and/or flutter suppression must comply with the control system stability requirements as agreed by the Certifying Authority.
(j) The flight control system must have a comprehensive self-test available and operating during all phases of flight, including preflight.

See AMC.U1330 (e), AMC.U1330 (i) and AMC.U1330 (j) The flight control system comprises sensors, actuators, computers and all those elements of the UAS, necessary to control the attitude, speed and trajectory of the UA. The flight control system must meet the following:
(a) The modes of control of the UAS must be the following categories, which may be selected at any time in flight by the UAS crew:
  (1) automatic: in this mode the UA attitude, speed and flight path are fully controlled by the flight control system. No input from the UCS is needed other than to load or modify the required flight plan.
  (2) semi-automatic: with this type of control the UAS crew commands outer loop parameters such as altitude, heading and air speed. The flight control system operates the UA controls to achieve the commanded outer loop parameter value.
(b) The flight control system must be designed so that a UAS crew of average skill can operate the UAS with acceptable workload,
(c) The flight control system must apply limits to manoeuvres to keep the UA in the flight envelope protection as defined in USAR.U334
(d) The UAS crews must have the opportunity to intervene at any time during the flight to manage safe control of the UAS, except:
  (1) during emergency situations such as total loss of data link, (2) during launch phase before achieving the minimum safe flight parameters, (3) during landing phase after reaching the decision point as defined in USAR.U1490 and USAR.U1492, (4) for UA designed to be recovered by parachute, during the landing phase under parachute, (5) for rocket or catapult assisted take-off UAS, during the launch phase before reaching the limits specified in USAR.U282 (e) The flight control system must be designed and adjusted so that, within the range of adjustment (if any) available to UAS crew, it cannot produce an unsafe condition. (f) The flight control system must be designed so that a single malfunction will not produce a hardover signal. If the flight control system integrates signals from auxiliary controls or furnishes signals for operation of other equipment, positive interlocks and sequencing of engagement to prevent improper operation are required. (g) There must be protection against adverse interaction of integrated components, resulting from a malfunction. (h) Not applicable in this subpart. (see USAR.U1790 UAS mode of control indicator) (i) Use of active flight controls for load alleviation, stability augmentation, and/or flutter suppression must comply with the control system stability requirements as agreed with the Certifying Authority. (j) The flight control system must have a comprehensive self-test available and operating during all phases of flight, including preflight. (k) Data exchanged between components of the flight control system or received from components external to the flight control system must be verified for the integrity of the information prior to use. Information received from external sources must be verified within appropriate rate of change and range boundaries for the appropriate phase of flight before using in the computations.
